requiredFindings.problem: The r2 materialization plan gates the whole existing command_checks function on commands presence. That function also owns component-name and manifest-alias admission. Applying the stated gate would bypass duplicate-name/alias, reserved-name and different-identity live-name collision checks for every closure-only manifest, contrary to the unchanged DR-103 rules. A commandless grammar manifest with a name or alias in the supplied reserved/live set would receive no check from this owner. This is a defect in the proposed C2a instructions, not an observed runtime regression.

evidence.observation: command_checks begins by indexing m["commands"] unconditionally.

The same function builds keys from manifest.name, manifest.aliases and root-command aliases, refuses duplicate keys (257-266), checks reserved_names (268-270), and checks context.live_names for a different (stableId, provenance) (271-276). These are component-name admission checks as well as command checks.

Both validate and validate_inventory call validate_inner; command_checks is the only call in this owner that applies the supplied reserved_names and live_names context. The proposed presence gate skips that whole call for all four closure-only roles.

Component name and alias uniqueness against the reserved list and live identities is an admission rule. Cross-entry collisions apply to a different (stableId, provenance); the coexistence exception is retained. CR-1 does not override any of these rules.
Every other DR-103 manifest rule applies to every role alike.

Shape validation constrains name syntax and uniqueness within the aliases array. It cannot reject an alias equal to manifest.name or a name/alias in supplied reserved/live context. The independent schema audit does not execute these semantic admission checks.

fix.instruction: Make only command-tree validation conditional. Preserve the existing component-name and manifest-alias admission for every role, with the current different-(stableId, provenance) coexistence exception; do not read commands for closure-only roles. No completed-schema edit or additional parent override is needed.

exactReplacements.after: The command-tree-specific checks run only when commands is present, which the schema makes exactly role analyzer. Component-name and manifest-alias admission currently colocated at component_manifest.rs:257-276 remains mandatory for every role: form the name/alias set without reading commands for closure-only roles, reject duplicate keys and reserved-list collisions, and check live-name collisions against a different (stableId, provenance); analyzer also includes its mounted-root aliases as before. The executable-entrypoint check (line 337) applies to role analyzer only, while a closure-only entrypoint must name a regular-file entry directly (no symlink resolution); the closure-only roles require capabilities [] and permissions [].

exactReplacements.insert: - **CR-T9.** For every role, component-name and manifest-alias admission remains enforced independently of command-tree presence. A component name or alias colliding with the reserved list refuses RJ-2; an alias duplicating the component name refuses RJ-2; a name or alias colliding with a live entry of a different `(stableId, provenance)` refuses RJ-2. The same-`(stableId, provenance)` coexistence control still admits when all other rules pass. Closure-only controls have no `commands`; analyzer controls retain their required tree and mounted-root alias checks.

RF-CR1-1.resolution: LD-8 is a sound alternative to the r1 offered inert-metadata repair. The schema, SL:70 and DR103 fields/8 semantics all require commands absent for the four closure-only roles. No mandatory tree remains to be a root-command claim; declared commands refuses through the closed schema. Analyzer command-tree admission is unchanged and its pre-existing D4/EE-3b/EE-5a question is explicitly left to M3-D.

NB-CR1-1.resolution: LD-9, SL:70 and CR-T4 require closure-only entrypoints to name a regular-file entry directly, while preserving existing analyzer in-tree resolution and executable-target checks.

assessment.rfResolution: Resolved by removing the closure-only command tree, rather than interpreting it as inert metadata. The fourth string override explicitly qualifies DR103 fields/8 required:true; the selected executable schema enforces the role-scoped exception.
assessment.schema: The two oneOf branches are disjoint by required role. The root retains commands as an array of 1..4096 CommandSpec objects. Analyzer requires that member and retains its prior constraints. The closure-only branch types a present commands member as null, which cannot also satisfy the root array type, so absence is the only admitted spelling. This is a minimal lawful absence constraint in the generator's supported subset. The schema alone does not enforce the semantic capabilities/permissions/entrypoint rules, which remain C2a responsibilities.
